text.en: Human beings live in societies and depend on each other. Our lives are shaped by the past, by the land and weather around us, by the rules we follow and by how we earn and spend. Social science studies all these together.

In Grades 6 to 8 we explored social science through stories of people, places and events. In Grade 9 we pause to understand what social science truly means.
Human beings live in societies and depend on each other in many ways, so the study of society needs more than one point of view.
History studies how people and societies changed over time, using sources such as inscriptions, coins and books.
Geography studies the Earth, its landforms, climate and resources, and how people live with them.
Political science studies power, rules, government and citizens' rights and duties.
Economics studies how people produce, exchange and use goods and services when resources are limited.
These disciplines are connected. For example, a monsoon failure (geography) affects farm incomes (economics), government relief (political science) and migration (history).
Social science teaches us to ask questions, look at evidence and respect different views.

problem.en: Show how a drought links all four social sciences.

text.en: Geography: rainfall fails and crops dry.
Economics: farmers lose income and prices rise.
Political science: government announces relief; history shows earlier famines.

prompt.en: Name the four disciplines and the main question each asks.

requiredIdeas.en: Economics and political science: resources and power

points.en: Social science studies people in society.
History, geography, political science and economics are its main branches.
It builds questioning and evidence-based thinking.
